title: Phase 13 exit criteria (gate — closed by Greg, or by explicit delegation per ADR-0067)
description: Gate bead for Phase 13 — The embedder's contract (ADR-0079, accepted; phase opened by Greg 2026-10-25). Exit criteria ratified as written at the opening: (1) safe, attributable writes over the socket: parameterised queries over the daemon matching the CLI's --param on every type both can express, injection-shaped input binding literally (acetone-d5is.1); a caller-supplied author for commits through the CLI and the socket, and for annotated tags through the CLI (acetone-gid; the daemon has no tag verb); (2) the machine-readable contract fixed before it hardens: the change report's and the merge verb's conflict items carry typed keys, the report's change under a bumped, CHANGELOG'd report_version (acetone-y629); reader isolation during a write or merge documented in protocol.md and pinned by tests (acetone-d5is.2); a tested, task-oriented guide to parallel edges (acetone-d5is.3) and the merge-time discriminator-declaration hole closed (acetone-7qw.26); (3) recovery and operator UX: uncommitted workspace changes can be discarded through the CLI and the socket (acetone-omk); the Phase 12 demo findings acetone-00wh and acetone-7ldo closed. Every user-facing item reachable through the shipped interface (ADR-0054 corollary). Never closed on an agent's own initiative.

title: Phase 13 security review SHOULD-FIX: author whitespace and length, serve --help verbs
description: From the Phase 13 milestone security review (comment on acetone-d5is, 2026-11-03). (1) Signature::validate (acetone-store store.rs) accepts leading/trailing whitespace in author name/email, which git's reader trims, so stored != read back; refuse it (both CLI --author/GIT_AUTHOR_* and socket params.author). (2) No length cap on author name/email; one socket frame can commit a 15 MiB name. Cap each field. (3) serve --help omits the discard, report and schema verbs.
design: Signature::validate (the new-identity path: commit and tag writes, CLI and socket) gains two checks: no leading/trailing whitespace per field, and <=1024 bytes per field. validate_identity_fields (header-injection guard, also used by history rewrites of stored identities) is unchanged, so rewrites of existing commits are unaffected. Signature::parse trims name and email (spaces/tabs only for email, so control chars stay refused); GIT_AUTHOR_* is trimmed in the CLI; socket params.author is strict (invalid-author). serve --help verb list completed; help snapshot updated. Tests: store unit tests, socket refusals in authorship.rs (red-checked), env trimming unit test.
close_reason: Shipped in #315 (squash d058d4a): Signature::validate refuses a name/email with surrounding whitespace or over 1024 bytes (new-identity path only; history rewrites keep validate_identity_fields' header rules); Signature::parse trims both fields (email: spaces/tabs only), GIT_AUTHOR_* trimmed in the CLI, socket strict (invalid-author); serve --help lists schema, discard, report; protocol.md, manual CLI reference and CHANGELOG updated. Two review rounds; the round-1 finding was the manual paragraph.

title: Write a task-oriented guide to parallel edges (manual guide + protocol note)
description: Tenant ask (priority 3): expose parallel edges (same predicate, same pair, different provenance), which 'may only mean surfacing the discriminator the format already reserves'. Verified 2026-10-24: shipped in 0.5 (acetone-o8r; PRs #251/#252). Declared discriminators work through schema apply, CREATE/MERGE, reads, import --disc and the report's disc field. The manual's CLI reference documents them (docs/manual/src/reference/cli.md, around lines 264-279), the glossary defines 'discriminator', and CHANGELOG 0.5.0 describes them. The gap is narrower than 'undiscoverable': there is no task-oriented guide, and docs/protocol.md never mentions discriminators.
design: Write a task-oriented 'Parallel relationships' guide in the manual's guide section, linked from docs/user-guide.md. Cross-link the existing reference text rather than duplicating it. Cover: declaring a discriminator with schema apply (and why declare-rel-type deliberately cannot); CREATE/MERGE behaviour (different values coexist; the same value is refused as a duplicate; null or absent is refused); SET/REMOVE of the discriminator refused as an identity change; import --disc; how diff, report and export show the discriminator; and the merge caveat until acetone-7qw.26 lands. In protocol.md, note that edges in rows and in the report carry the discriminator. Exercise every example in a doc test or CLI integration test so the guide cannot rot.
acceptance_criteria: A reader of the manual's guide alone, reached from docs/user-guide.md, can declare, create, query, edit and import parallel edges. Every example is exercised by a test. protocol.md notes the discriminator on edges.

PHASE 13 OPENED by Greg on 2026-10-25: the phase-start guard above is lifted; this bead may be claimed (ADR-0079).

title: Phase 13 — The embedder's contract (ADR-0079)
description:
Phase 13 epic, OPEN since 2026-10-25 (opened by Greg first-hand in session; verbatim instruction in this epic's comments). Proposed 2026-10-24 by the define-the-next-phase grooming session (PR #296). Theme, membership, exit criteria and opening rulings per ADR-0079 (docs/adr/0079-phase-13-embedders-contract.md) and the roadmap's Phase 13 section. Size M, target version 0.8.

Strands: (1) safe, attributable writes over the socket — Cypher parameter binding on the daemon's query verb; caller-supplied commit/tag author identity (commits via CLI and socket, annotated tags via CLI; GIT_AUTHOR_* fallback in the CLI only); (2) the machine-readable contract fixed before it hardens — typed conflict keys in the change report (report_version 2), the reader-isolation guarantee documented and test-pinned, parallel edges documented end to end with the merge-time discriminator hole closed; (3) recovery and operator UX — workspace discard through CLI and socket, the Phase 12 demo's help/log findings. Housekeeping riding the phase: a Linux row for the protocol measurement. Left out at the opening: EXPLAIN (acetone-a9m) and the relay re-pin (acetone-d5is.4, closed).

Membership note: acetone-omk (parent acetone-2ck) and acetone-7qw.26 (parent acetone-7qw) are joined by dependency and the phase-13 label, not reparented — a cloud session's relay cannot remove their existing parent link. acetone-a9m still carries the phase-13 label but is out of the phase; remove the label from a local session.
notes: Revised after PR #296's adversarial review (2026-10-24): tags over the socket descoped (no daemon tag verb); the daemon never reads ambient author identity; the parameter channel specified as a new JSON mapping; the merge verb's conflict payload brought into acetone-y629; acetone-a9m joins by label only.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Phase 13 milestone security review (fresh subagent, ae918a6..c81715f, 2026-11-03). Verdict: no BLOCKERs; gate can close on security grounds. SHOULD-FIX: (1) Signature::validate accepts leading/trailing whitespace in author name/email; the raw commit keeps it but read_commit/log trim it, so stored != read back and a history rewrite does not reproduce the identity exactly (not header injection; git fsck --strict clean); CLI parse trims name but not email. (2) No length cap on author name/email: one 16 MiB socket frame committed a 15 MiB author name, permanent history bloat re-read per log --json row. (3) serve --help omits the discard, report and schema verbs. NOTES (accepted): json_params refuses integral floats >= 2^63 (documented; message says 'integer'); parameter nesting bounded by serde_json's 128 depth; non-UTF-8 GIT_AUTHOR_* read as unset; report::conflict_items indexes fields[name] (no reachable panic, builder always sets keys); socket discard drops every connection's staged writes (documented, gated, refused mid-merge incl. half-aborted); missed object lookups retry twice at 1 ms (misses only). Checked sound: identity header injection (control chars, <, > refused on every path), neutral committer, frame sync on import author errors, parameter names, crash-safe abort, discriminator stability at declare/merge/import, merge determinism (format_version 1 holds), derived maps under discard, pack retirement order, no new crates, scripts use argv-only subprocess.

title: Crash between abort_merge's workspace reset and MERGE_HEAD delete leaves a stray MERGE_HEAD; next commit records a merge
description: Found while pinning the abort_merge ref window (acetone-d5is.2, PR #304). If the process dies after the workspace CAS but before MERGE_HEAD is deleted, recovery leaves MERGE_HEAD over a clean workspace, so a following commit records a two-parent merge commit. Pre-existing. Fix: on detecting MERGE_HEAD with a workspace equal to HEAD's tree and no conflicts, treat the merge as aborted (or make commit refuse and point at merge --abort); pin with a test that rebuilds the half-aborted state.
close_reason: Shipped in #312 (squash 7e54d20): abort_merge now marks a fully resolved merge with an empty conflicts map, deletes MERGE_HEAD, then resets the workspace, all under the WriteLock, so a crash at any point leaves a state the next commit completes or a re-run merge --abort finishes; the old-order stray state is still recovered by abort. Deviation from the first design, from review: save_in_place refuses every write while a conflicts map stands with no MERGE_HEAD (naming merge --abort), so a write cannot clear the mark. protocol.md documents that status shows a dirty workspace with no merge block in that window. No format change.

title: Declare-time discriminator gaps: new rel type declared with a discriminator over stored edges; rel-type entry deletion unchecked
description: Surfaced by acetone-7qw.26 (PR #303). (1) check_rel_disc_stability lets a relationship type that is new to the schema be declared with a discriminator over edges already stored under that type (the stability check only compares against a previously declared entry). (2) Deleting a relationship-type entry is not checked against existing edges. Both are declare-time siblings of the merge-time check #303 adds; fix by mirroring the same stale-discriminator rule at declare time.
close_reason: Shipped in #311 (squash 7791d99): check_rel_disc_stability treats an absent rtype entry as declaring no discriminator, so declaring a discriminator for a new type over stored edges, or deleting an entry that declared one, is a change; a change is refused when an edge of that type survives from the old edge map (provenance, as ADR-0082), so a change riding with the deletion of every edge it would falsify lands. Deviation from the first design, from review: rename_rel_type's reconcile step now treats an absent declaration the same way and refuses (RelTypeRenameConflict) a one-sided rename that would put an undeclared side's edges under a declared discriminator, in both directions.

title: Report v2 follow-ups from PR #301 review: docs, comments and violation/schema item tests
description: Non-blocking findings from the PR #301 (acetone-y629) review, to close in Phase 13 (ADR-0054): (1) report v2 renders bytes/temporal base/ours/theirs values through value_to_json ({"$type": ...}), consistent with nodes[].properties but not stated in the CHANGELOG entry or protocol.md's report version history; state it. (2) docs/protocol.md: the new 'The change report' section sits above the Verbs section's 'An unknown verb is a typed unknown-verb error...' paragraph; move the section below it. (3) report.rs: comments implying a serialised key order (serde_json emits keys alphabetically) are misleading; reword. (4) serve.rs merge verb: if conflict_items fails after the merge entered merge-in-progress the client gets an error frame though state changed; consider an ok frame noting the failure, or document. (5) manual history chapter prose does not mention the new entity column. (6) add automated report tests for a graph-violation item (dangling-edge) and a schema-key item; both were verified by hand in review.
close_reason: Shipped in #313 (squash eee88d3): protocol.md and CHANGELOG document the report's tagged value forms, sorted item keys and the merge verb's report-error case (documented rather than reshaped, as the bead allowed); the unknown-verb paragraph returned to Verbs; the manual explains the conflicts entity column; a CLI test covers dangling-edge and schema-key conflict items. No deviations.

title: CLI help omits ancestry refspecs (main~1, HEAD^) shipped in #284
description:
Component: the help strings in `crates/acetone-cli/src/cli.rs`. Found in Phase 12 demo step 6.

Since 0.7 (acetone-bvq, #284), git ancestry refspecs (`main~N`, `HEAD^`, `^N`) resolve everywhere a refspec is accepted. Every refspec help string still says only "branch/tag short name, full ref name or commit hash":
- `branch [REFSPEC]` (~l.160)
- `tag [REFSPEC]` (~l.190)
- `diff FROM TO` (l.216)
- `merge REF` (~l.261)
- `schema --at` (l.361/367)
- `query --at` (l.458)

This is the same kind of staleness that #292 fixed in spec §5.2.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each refspec help string mentions the ancestry syntax.
- The help for `report`, `blame` and `serve`, and the manual, are checked for the same phrase and fixed.

title: Add acetone log --oneline
description:
Component: `acetone log`, and possibly `acetone blame`. Found in Phase 12 demo step 6, where the demo had to fake compact output with `cut`.

`log` has only `--all` and `--json`, so there is no compact form. Users with git habits reach for `--oneline` first.

Design points:
- Interaction with `--all`: should merge commits show their parent hashes?
- Make it mutually exclusive with `--json`.
- Consider the same flag for `blame`.

A candidate for next grooming, not a blocker.
acceptance_criteria:
- `--oneline` prints an abbreviated hash and the subject per commit, with trailers suppressed.
- It is rejected together with `--json`.

title: CLI: workspace discard / restore (checkout refuses even current branch when dirty)
description: PR #178: there is no way to throw away uncommitted workspace changes from the CLI; checkout refuses when dirty even for the current branch. Operators need acetone checkout --discard (or restore). Feature -> Phase 9 unless trivially small.
design: Phase 13 scope (ADR-0079, proposed; gate-bearing). A host that abandons a failed batch has no way back: there is no discard over the socket at all. Interface: 'acetone discard' resets the workspace to HEAD's committed manifest, plus a matching daemon 'discard' verb. During a merge in progress it refuses and advises merge --abort. The merge-in-progress check MUST run under the same WriteLock as the reset. reset_workspace_to_head takes the lock itself, so a check made before calling it is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap; refactor to an inner unlocked variant called under one lock. CAS on the workspace ref. Shared workspace: under the daemon's model, one connection's discard throws away every connection's staged writes. Document this in protocol.md and test it (coordinate with acetone-d5is.2). Recommendation: checking out the current branch while dirty stays refused, since discard is the explicit verb. Tests: dirty -> discard -> status clean, via the CLI and the socket; refused mid-merge; a concurrent writer gets 'locked'; derived maps (edges_rev, indexes) equal HEAD's (Invariant 5). Update protocol.md, the Python client and the user guide.
